newsitem.title: CHINA: MORTGAGE CORP SETS OUT BUYING CRITERIA.
newsitem.headline: MORTGAGE CORP SETS OUT BUYING CRITERIA.

text.p: The new body set up to prevent a HK$788 billion shortfall in Hong Kong's mortgage market has spelt out its buying criteria for banks.
In a notice to banks, the Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC), set out maximum and minimum mortgage sizes, credit criteria and permissible maturities on mortgages it buys from banks.
HKMC chief operating officer Leland Sun said the maximum size of an individual loan is HK$8 million when originated.
He said the maximum permissible that could be owed on a mortgage is HK$5 million, and the minimum HK$300,000.
The HKMC plans to buy home mortgages to relieve pressure on those banks nearing lending limits on home loans because of a ballooning appetite for mortgage finance.
If nothing is done, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) predicts a HK$788 billion gap between available mortgage funding and consumer demand early next century.
Sun said the maximum loan-to-valuation ratio at the time the mortgage is written can be no more than 70 percent, and the maximum debt-to-household income ratio 50 percent.
Mortgages must have been seasoned for at least one year, and not have more than a 30-year term when written, he said.
Home loans should not be concentrated in a single development or location, and should be owner-occupied, he said.
The corporation requires a "clear record" on mortgage payments in the 12 months before the mortgage is sold to the HKMC and mortgaged properties must be adequately insured.
He said the criteria only apply to private residential properties, and different criteria will be set for government assisted programmes for home buyers.
